clue.text: Dance tango in New Orleans after church

indicators.note: the remade letters come after the church abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the city's letters with the added one are set out afresh

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dances a tango in New Orleans after the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city's name, but 'New' is the signal to rearrange ORLEANS with the T put in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s jazz-age dance named after the South Carolina city.

clue.text: Economic collapse wiping out Republican money

indicators.note: wiping something out removes it, so the party letter is taken away

parts.note: a crash is a sudden collapse of markets
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A financial crash wipes out the Republicans' funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is a general synonym for money, especially in notes and coins.

clue.text: Hardy companion, eschewing starter, eats fresh tuna plainly cooked

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself
to eschew the starter is to go without the first letter

parts.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so the fish's letters are made into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hardy's companion skips the first course and eats fresh tuna, simply prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were the classic comedy double act, so 'Hardy companion' is Stan Laurel; the shortened name then wraps round the reworked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel is French for 'in the natural state', used of food served or cooked simply without dressing.

clue.text: Character synonymous with a fan of drama

definitions.text: Character synonymous with a fan of drama

parts.words: Character synonymous with a fan of drama
parts.note: surface reading: a person whose name is a byword for an enthusiast of the theatre
setter's reading: the fan is the hand-held object in a play's title, and the character is the one who owns it

explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's comedy is titled after this woman's fan, so her name goes with that fan wherever the play is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the heroine of Wilde's play, whose title is named for her fan, an accessory central to the plot.

clue.text: Yours truly absorbing large, decisive blow

indicators.note: absorbing something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the crossword's compiler refers to themself as the setter
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: I take a heavy, decisive punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is an informal word for a final blow or argument that settles a matter.

clue.text: Waterproof paint layer

parts.note: oil paint, or oils, used by artists
a skin is a thin outer layer

explanation.surface: A waterproof coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof garment of cloth treated with oil, so the noun names the waterproof itself.

clue.text: Swish hotel taken over by top military bod

indicators.note: to be taken over by something is to be swallowed up within it

parts.note: C-in-C, the commander-in-chief
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A smart hotel is commandeered by a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The commander-in-chief is abbreviated C-in-C, written CIC here, which holds the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is British informal for fashionably smart, which is what chic means.

clue.text: Capital head regularly censored best-selling single

indicators.note: censoring at regular intervals cuts every other letter, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: first and third letters kept
a number one, written NO 1, with 1 as I

explanation.surface: The capital's top official keeps banning a hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Fruit left in bond at home by European

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces stand next to one another
one letter is placed inside the word for bond

parts.note: to cement is to bond things together
L is the abbreviation for left
someone at home is in
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Fruit left inside a binding agreement at home by someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small seedless citrus fruit, a hybrid of mandarin and orange.

clue.text: Might one scoff at this during pillow talk?

definitions.text: Might one scoff at this during pillow talk?

parts.words: Might one scoff at this during pillow talk?
parts.note: surface reading: someone sneering at intimate words whispered in bed
setter's reading: scoff means eat greedily, and the pillows place the meal in the bedroom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff at' looks like mockery, but scoff is British slang for eating, and pillow talk only tells you where the eating happens.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a morning meal taken while still lying among the pillows, a classic treat on a special day.

clue.text: Both sides in Salisbury getting agreement for clerical gathering

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its two edges, so only its first and last letters count

parts.note: first and last letters
a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: Both factions in Salisbury, a cathedral city, reach agreement at a church meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church officials meeting to decide church matters.

clue.text: Play part killing Romeo in a dazed state

indicators.note: the shortened part sits inside the dazed state

parts.note: a trance is a half-conscious dazed condition

indicators.note: killing a letter does away with it, so it is removed

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor's part kills Romeo while he is in a stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play part' reads like acting, but 'Play' alone is the definition, in its engineering sense of slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Play means the slack or allowed freedom of movement in a mechanism, which engineers call tolerance.

clue.text: Ordering Lancelot a Kiwi-English or Australian novel

indicators.note: ordering puts things into a sequence, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Bossing Lancelot around, a New Zealander, an Englishman or an Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi is a nickname for a New Zealander, but here it is just four letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Town Like Alice is Nevil Shute's 1950 novel set partly in the Australian outback town of Alice Springs.

clue.text: Expert son training American spies on record

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means sitting above, so the spies come before the record

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
PE is physical education, i.e. physical training
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: An expert's son trains American spies, all on file.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is a person with expert knowledge of one particular field.

clue.text: Spouse Catherine who survived grappling with Stanley occasionally

indicators.note: a wrestler grappling with someone wraps arms around them

parts.note: Catherine Parr, Henry VIII's sixth wife, outlived him

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the name is used

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A spouse called Catherine, who lived through it all, wrestles with Stanley now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Of Henry VIII's six wives, Catherine Parr is the one remembered as 'survived'.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a spouse or long-term companion in a marriage or similar relationship.

clue.text: Most tasteless supporter backed celebratory gathering

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the supporter's word is read from its end

parts.note: a fan supports a team or star
a fest is a festival or party

explanation.surface: The tackiest fan threw their money behind the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for lacking style, so the superlative means most tasteless.

clue.text: Had meal following end of office work in the US? Fancy!

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the meal piece goes at the end
the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: last letter
American spelling of labour
past tense of eat

explanation.surface: An American eats after finishing at the office: how about that!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' sounds like an exclamation of surprise, but it is the adjective meaning intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy and elaborate both describe something highly decorated or intricately detailed.

clue.text: Roughly stuffing tree in crater

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so one word is packed inside the other

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: A tree is roughly crammed into a crater.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large basin-shaped volcanic crater formed by collapse after an eruption.

clue.text: With which to pick up a northern male voice on the radio?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the device rather than a synonym

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: what is on the radio is heard rather than read, so the voice's word goes by its spoken form

parts.note: a tenor is the high adult male voice; in non-rhotic speech it ends like this spelling

explanation.surface: How a northern tenor's singing reaches you over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an antenna is the thing you use to pick up signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial, the device that receives radio and television signals.

clue.text: Scorn and loudly traduce a Scandinavian

indicators.note: loudly means said out for hearing, so the spoken sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to diss is to insult or traduce, and a Dane is from Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a Scandinavian and runs them down at the top of their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for contempt, as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Writer's hell nursing broken neck

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one word cradles the other

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's agony of caring for a broken neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hell' tempts as the answer itself (what the dickens), but it gives DIS, the Roman underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens was the Victorian novelist, so the surname stands for a writer.

clue.text: George being one involved in gun conspiracy

parts.note: an automatic is a self-loading firearm

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: George is one of those caught up in an armed conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: George was RAF slang for the autopilot, so the name is the definition, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots nicknamed the aircraft's self-steering system George, making it a fair slang synonym for the device.

clue.text: Nobs, very loud, turned up drunk outside

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top
the drunk's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
fortissimo in music

explanation.surface: Rowdy upper-class types turn up drunk out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Nob and toff are both British slang for posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs and nobs are British slang for wealthy, upper-class people.

clue.text: York Stadium?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, to york a batsman is to deliver a ball that lands at his feet
second meaning: a ...-shaped sports arena, like the Hollywood ...

explanation.walkthrough: York looks like the city with its stadium; in cricket a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet, so to york is a way to deliver the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to deliver a ball in cricket, and also a large round amphitheatre for sport or concerts.

clue.text: Meddling when abandoning short term, in conclusion

indicators.note: abandoning something leaves it behind, so those letters are dropped
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: interference is meddling
the word cut short

explanation.surface: Meddling stops at the end of a short school term, to conclude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conclusion' sounds like a sign-off, but the definition is just 'conclusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inference is a conclusion reached by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Party head last seen in Truro

parts.note: bean is slang for the head

indicators.note: the last thing seen in a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: The party leader was last spotted in Truro, a Cornish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British informal for a lively party or celebration, originally a works outing.

clue.text: Starts to throw out some household rubbish

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters

explanation.surface: Begin throwing away some of the domestic junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British informal for nonsense, a sense of rubbish meaning foolish talk.

clue.text: Er, Delilah's gone mad — kicked up a terrible stink

indicators.note: something gone mad is wildly disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Delilah has lost her temper and made a huge fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delilah's' reads as possessive but is 'Delilah is', and its S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for protesting loudly and angrily, just as kicking up a stink is.
